pr_title: executor: parallelize aggregations with distinct in hashAgg
pr_body:
<!-- Thank you for contributing to TiDB!

PR Title Format:

2. *: what's changed

-->

### What problem does this PR solve?

Issue Number: close #17075 <!-- REMOVE this line if no issue to close -->

Problem Summary:

``` sql
select count(distinct a) from t;
```

If one of the aggregate functions in a query needs distinct evaluation, the hashAgg executor will run in single thread.

### What is changed and how it works?

What's Changed:

- HashAgg executor will execute aggregation functions with distinct (without order by) in parallel instead of in single thread.

How it Works:

- modify the structures of `partialResult4XXXDistinct`s to store ordered distinct values
- add aggregation functions with distinct and methods `MergePartialResult` for final workers in order to merge the results of partial workers correctly.

### Related changes

- Need to cherry-pick to the release branch 3.0, 4.0

### Check List <!--REMOVE the items that are not applicable-->

Tests <!-- At least one of them must be included. -->

- Unit test
- Integration test

Side effects

- Performance regression
    - Consumes more CPU
    - Consumes more MEM

issue_context.title: Parallel evaluation for aggregate functions with distinct in hashAgg
issue_context.body:
## Development Task

```mysql
select count(distinct a) from t;
```


Currently if one of the aggregate functions of a SQL has a distinct evaluation, the `hashAgg` executor must run in a single thread. See https://github.com/pingcap/tidb/blob/3224393/executor/builder.go#L1207

We may find a method to evaluate it in parallel, maybe a `sync.Map` for deduplicating entries can be shared in multiple goroutines.

review_comments: `MergePartialResult` is single-thread, this heavy calculation should be avoided.
